"Uniform fair dice" are dice where all faces have an equal probability of outcome due to the symmetry of the die as it is [face-transitive](/wiki/Isohedral_figure "Isohedral figure"). In addition to the Platonic solids, these theoretically include:

* [Catalan solids](/wiki/Catalan_solid "Catalan solid"), the [duals](/wiki/Dual_polyhedron "Dual polyhedron") of the 13 [Archimedean solids](/wiki/Archimedean_solid "Archimedean solid"): 12, 24, 30, 48, 60, 120 sides
* [Trapezohedra](/wiki/Trapezohedron "Trapezohedron"), the duals of the infinite set of [antiprisms](/wiki/Antiprism "Antiprism"), with kite faces: any even number not divisible by 4 (so that a facet faces up), starting from 6
* [Bipyramids](/wiki/Bipyramid "Bipyramid"), the duals of the infinite set of [prisms](/wiki/Prism_(geometry) "Prism (geometry)"), with triangle faces: any multiple of 4 (so that a facet faces up), starting from 8
* [Disphenoids](/wiki/Disphenoid "Disphenoid"), an infinite set of tetrahedra made from congruent non-regular triangles: 4 sides. This is a less symmetric tetrahedron than the Platonic tetrahedron but still sufficiently symmetrical to be face-transitive. Similarly, [pyritohedra](/wiki/Pyritohedron "Pyritohedron") and [tetartoids](/wiki/Tetartoid "Tetartoid") are less symmetrical but still face-transitive dodecahedra: 12 sides.

Two other types of polyhedra are technically not face-transitive but are still fair dice due to symmetry:

* [antiprisms](/wiki/Antiprism "Antiprism"): the basis of [barrel dice](/wiki/Barrel_dice "Barrel dice")
* [prisms](/wiki/Prism_(geometry) "Prism (geometry)"): the basis of long dice and teetotums

During the [Pacific War](/wiki/Pacific_War "Pacific War"), Mahito Maki loses his hospitalized mother, Hisako, in a fire. Mahito's father Shoichi, an [air munitions factory](/wiki/Arsenal "Arsenal") owner, [marries his late wife's sister](/wiki/Sororate_marriage "Sororate marriage"), Natsuko, and they evacuate to her rural estate. Mahito, distant to the pregnant Natsuko, encounters a peculiar [grey heron](/wiki/Grey_heron "Grey heron") leading him to a sealed tower, the last known location of Natsuko's architect granduncle.

After a school fight, Mahito [deliberately injures himself](/wiki/Self-harm "Self-harm"). The heron, now speaking, entices Mahito with promises of finding his mother. Mahito is nearly kidnapped by a swarm of creatures, but Natsuko saves him with a [whistling arrow](/wiki/Whistling_arrow "Whistling arrow"), inspiring him to craft his own bow and arrow. The arrow is magically imbued with true aim after it is [fletched](/wiki/Fletching "Fletching") with the heron's feather. Mahito's reading of [a book](/wiki/How_Do_You_Live%3F "How Do You Live?") left by Hisako is interrupted when an ill Natsuko disappears into the forest. Leading one of the estate's elderly maids, Kiriko, into the tower, Mahito is deceived by a watery imitation of his mother made by the heron, which dissolves at his touch. Affronted, he pierces the heron's beak with his arrow, revealing a flightless creature, the Birdman, living inside it. A wizard appears, ordering the Birdman to guide Mahito and Kiriko as all three sink into the floor.

Mahito descends into an oceanic world. He is rescued from attacking pelicans and a forbidding, [megalithic](/wiki/Megalith "Megalith") [dolmen](/wiki/Dolmen "Dolmen") by a younger Kiriko, an adept fisherwoman who uses fire through a magic wand. Lindenstrauss was born into an Israeli-Jewish family with [German Jewish](/wiki/German_Jews "German Jews") origins, the son of the mathematician [Joram Lindenstrauss](/wiki/Joram_Lindenstrauss "Joram Lindenstrauss"), the namesake of the [Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma](/wiki/Johnson%E2%80%93Lindenstrauss_lemma "Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma"), and computer scientist Naomi Lindenstrauss, both professors at the [Hebrew University of Jerusalem](/wiki/Hebrew_University_of_Jerusalem "Hebrew University of Jerusalem"). His sister Ayelet Lindenstrauss is also a mathematician. He attended the [Hebrew University Secondary School](/wiki/Hebrew_University_Secondary_School "Hebrew University Secondary School"). In 1988 he was awarded a bronze medal at the International Mathematical Olympiad. He enlisted to the [IDF](/wiki/Israel_Defense_Forces "Israel Defense Forces")'s [Talpiot program](/wiki/Talpiot_program "Talpiot program") and studied at the [Hebrew University of Jerusalem](/wiki/Hebrew_University_of_Jerusalem "Hebrew University of Jerusalem"), where he earned his BSc in [Mathematics](/wiki/Mathematics "Mathematics") and [Physics](/wiki/Physics "Physics") in 1991 and his master's degree in mathematics in 1995. In 1999 he finished his Ph.D., his thesis being "Entropy properties of dynamical systems", under the guidance of Prof. Benjamin Weiss. He was a member at the [Institute for Advanced Study](/wiki/Institute_for_Advanced_Study "Institute for Advanced Study") in [Princeton, New Jersey](/wiki/Princeton,_New_Jersey "Princeton, New Jersey"), then a Szego Assistant Prof. at [Stanford University](/wiki/Stanford_University "Stanford University"). From 2003 to 2005, he was a Long Term Prize Fellow at the [Clay Mathematics Institute](/wiki/Clay_Mathematics_Institute "Clay Mathematics Institute").
